Hamiltonian mechanics: equations of motion, Poisson brackets, canonical transformations, Hamilton-Jacobi theory, action-angle variables, adiabatic invariants.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Mathematical Methods for Physics
courses.description: An introduction to mathematical methods used in theoretical physics. Topics include a review of complex variable theory, applications of the Cauchy residue theorem, asymptotic series, method of steepest descent, Fourier and Laplace transforms, series solutions for ODE’s and related special functions, Sturm Liouville theory, variational principles, boundary value problems, and Green’s function techniques.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Nonequilibrium Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Transport phenomena; kinetic theory and the Chapman-Enskog method; hydrodynamic theory; nonlinear effects and the mode coupling method. Stochastic processes; Langevin and Fokker-Planck equation; fluctuation-dissipation relation; multiplicative processes; dynamic field theory; Martin-Siggia-Rose formalism; dynamical scaling theory.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 210A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Solid-State Physics I
courses.description: The first of a two-quarter course in solid-state physics. Covers a range of solid-state phenomena that can be understood within an independent particle description. Topics include chemical versus band-theoretical description of solids, electronic band structure calculation, lattice dynamics, transport phenomena and electrodynamics in metals, optical properties, semiconductor physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics I
courses.description: Quantum principles of state (pure, composite, entangled, mixed), observables, time evolution, and measurement postulate. Simple soluble systems: two-state, harmonic oscillator, and spherical potentials. Angular momentum and spin. Time-independent approximations.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Fields I
courses.description: Introduction to field quantization for relativistic scalar, Fermion, and gauge fields. Symmetries and conservation laws. Calculation of cross sections and reaction rates via perturbation theory and Feynman diagram methods, including for tree-level processes in quantum electrodynamics.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 212C.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Fluid Dynamics for Physicists
courses.description: This is a basic course in fluid dynamics for advanced students. The course consists of core fundamentals and modules on advanced applications to physical and biological phenomena. Core fundamentals include Euler and Navier-Stokes equations, potential and Stokesian flow, instabilities, boundary layers, turbulence, and shocks. Module topics include MHD, waves, and the physics of locomotion and olfaction. May be coscheduled with PHYS 116. The performance criteria for graduate students will be to complete and pass (1) a graduate-level exam and (2) graduate-level homework problem sets. In both cases, there will be overlap with the undergraduate exam and problems, but the graduates will be expected to complete additional work at a higher level. Recommended preparation: prior coursework consistent with PHYS 100B and 110B content. Open to major codes PY75, PY76, PY77, PY78, PY79, PY80, PY81, and PY82 only. All others must use the Enrollment Authorization System (EASy) to request approval to enroll.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Condensed Matter/Materials Science Laboratory
courses.description: A project-oriented laboratory course utilizing state-of-the-art experimental techniques in materials science. The course prepares students for research in a modern condensed matter-materials science laboratory. Under supervision, the students develop their own experimental ideas after investigating current research literature. With the use of sophisticated state-of-the-art instrumentation students conduct research, write a research paper, and make verbal presentations.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 211A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Group Theoretical Methods in Physics
courses.description: Study of group theoretical methods with applications to problems in high energy, atomic, and condensed matter physics. Representation theory, tensor methods, Clebsh-Gordan series. Young tableaux. The course will cover discrete groups, Lie groups and Lie algebras, with emphasis on permutation, orthogonal, and unitary groups.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 212C.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: General Relativity
courses.description: This is a two-quarter course on gravitation and the general theory of relativity. The first quarter is intended to be offered every year and may be taken independently of the second quarter. The second quarter will be offered in alternate years. Topics covered in the first quarter include special relativity, differential geometry, the equivalence principle, the Einstein field equations, and experimental and observational tests of gravitation theories. The second quarter will focus on more advanced topics, including gravitational collapse, Schwarzschild and Kerr geometries, black holes, gravitational radiation, cosmology, and quantum gravitation.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: From time to time a member of the regular faculty or a resident visitor will find it possible to give a self-contained short course on an advanced topic in his or her special area of research. This course is not offered on a regular basis, but it is estimated that it will be given once each academic year. (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Condensed Matter Physics Seminar
courses.description: Discussion of current research in physics of the solid state and of other condensed matter. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: High-Energy Physics Seminar
courses.description: Discussions of current research in nuclear physics, principally in the field of elementary particles. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Plasma Physics Seminar
courses.description: Discussions of recent research in plasma physics. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Astrophysics and Cosmology Seminar
courses.description: Discussions of recent research in astrophysics and cosmology. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Biophysics Seminar
courses.description: Presentation of current research in biological physics and quantitative biology by invited speakers from the United States and abroad. (S/U grades only.) May be taken for credit thirty times.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Biophysics Research Talks
courses.description: Discussion of recent research in biological physics and quantitative biology by current graduate students. (S/U grades only.) May be taken for credit thirty times.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Colloquium
courses.description: Discussions of recent research in physics directed to the entire physics community. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Biological Physics
courses.description: The course teaches how a few fundamental models from statistical physics provide quantitative explanatory frameworks for many seemingly unrelated problems in biology. Case studies rotate from year to year and may include ion channel gating, cooperative binding, protein-DNA interaction, gene regulation, molecular motor dynamics, cytoskeletal assembly, biological electricity, population and evolutionary dynamics. May be coscheduled with PHYS 175. Students in PHYS 275 are expected to complete a report at the level of a research paper. Recommended preparation: an introduction to statistical mechanics, at least at the level of PHYS 140A or CHEM 132.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Neurodynamics
courses.description: Introduction to the nonlinear dynamics of neurons and simple neural systems through nonlinear dynamics, bifurcation theory, and chaotic motions. The dynamics of single cells is considered at different levels of abstraction, e.g., biophysical and “reduced” models for analysis of regularly spiking and bursting cells, their dynamical properties, and their representation in phase space. Laboratory exercises will accompany the lectures. Duplicate credit not allowed for cross-listed courses: BGGN 260, BENG 260, PHYS 279.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Biological Systems
courses.description: The course will introduce basic concepts of dynamical systems, from low dimensional systems to spatially extended systems, including Fisher wave, Turing instability, and excitable systems, and apply them to the study of concrete biological systems taken from a spectrum of fields including ecology and developmental biology. Recommended preparation: basic knowledge of biology and partial differential equations. A first course in partial differential equations; some basic concepts of modern biology.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Directed Study in Physics
courses.description: Research studies under the direction of a faculty member. (S/U grades only.) May be taken for credit up to twenty-four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: instructor and department approval required.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Thesis Research in Physics
courses.description: Directed research on dissertation topic. (S/U grades only.) May be taken for credit up to twenty-four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: instructor and department approval required.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Instruction in Physics Teaching
courses.description: This course, designed for graduate students, includes discussion of teaching, techniques and materials necessary to teach physics courses. One meeting per week with course instructors, one meeting per week in an assigned recitation section, problem session, or laboratory section. Students are required to take a total of two units of PHYS 500.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Race and Ethnicity in American Politics
courses.description: This course examines the processes by which racial and ethnic groups have/have not been incorporated into the American political system. The course focuses on the political experiences of European immigrant groups, blacks, Latinos, and Asians.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Participation and Inequality
courses.description: This course examines the causes and consequences of the unequal participation and representation of groups in U.S. politics.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Organized Interests
courses.description: This course provides a theoretical and practical examination of political parties, interest groups, and social movements in the United States.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Black Politics in the US
courses.description: Course will provide a comprehensive overview of Black politics in the United States by examining prominent racial social movements, Black public opinion and political behavior, the challenges and opportunities for Black elected officials, the significance of Black representation in government, and how race intersects with gender, age, and class to influence the salience of identity and the political behavior of African Americans.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The Supreme Court and the Constitution
courses.description: An introduction to the study of the Supreme Court and constitutional doctrine. Topics will include the nature of judicial review, federalism, race, and equal protection. The relation of judicial and legislative power will also be examined.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Race and Law
courses.description: Has the law helped end or contributed to racism in the United States? This course will explore the law of Slavery, Segregation, and Immigration, and study Equal Protection, Affirmative Action, and Criminal Justice (including hate crimes and First Amendment implications).

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Citizens and Saints: Political Thought from Plato to Augustine
courses.description: This course focuses on the development of politics and political thought in ancient Greece, its evolution through Rome and the rise of Christianity. Readings from Plato, Aristotle, Augustine, Machiavelli, and others.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Abuse of Power
courses.description: Power, a crucial part of politics, can be, and often is, abused. This course discusses the nature of power and surveys a variety of abuses, including agenda manipulation, rent extraction, fraud, extortion, corruption, exploitation, and gross political oppression.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The Politics of Food in a Global Economy
courses.description: This course explores emerging issues in production and consumption of food in a global economy. On production side, we discuss issues such as famine, overproduction of commercial crops, and sustainability. On consumption side, we explore issues such as fair trade, ethical consumption, and public health consequences (such as obesity). Then we discuss the roles of governments, international organizations, and communities to address these issues.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Corruption in Developing Countries
courses.description: This course explores corruption in developing countries. It examines various types of corruption in areas including health care, elections, natural resources, development projects, and international business. The course investigates causes and consequences of corruption, with an emphasis on political and economic factors. It also explores successes and failures of anti-corruption policies enacted by domestic and international actors. The course draws on examples from Africa, Asia, and Latin America.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Political Economy of Development
courses.description: Why are some countries rich and others poor? This course examines how political and economic factors shape development trajectories, focusing on Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Topics include the impact of democracy, corruption, oil, and foreign aid on economic development.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Japanese Politics: A Developmental Perspective
courses.description: This course will analyze the political systems of modern Japan in comparative-historical perspective.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Selected Topics in Latin American Politics
courses.description: A comparative analysis of contemporary political issues in Latin America. Material to be drawn from two or three countries. Among the topics: development, nationalism, neoimperialism, political change. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: War and Society
courses.description: How has warfighting evolved over the centuries? How has it varied across cultures? What has war been like for soldiers and civilians? How do societies mobilize for war, and how do they change in the short and long term from fighting?
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Relations After the Cold War: Theory and Prospect
courses.description: The nature of international politics appears to have changed dramatically since 1989. This course applies different theoretical approaches to enhance our understanding of the new international environment, future prospects for peace and war, and current problems of foreign policy.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Special Topics in International Relations
courses.description: An undergraduate course designed to cover various aspects of international relations. May be repeated for credit two times, provided each course is a separate topic, for a maximum of twelve units.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Analyzing Politics
courses.description: Politics are understood as the combination of individual preferences and decisions into collective choices. What are the issues involved in aggregating individual preferences, what is the choice of rules—formal and informal—for doing so.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Text as Data
courses.description: (Cross-listed with DSC 161.) This class explores statistical and computational methods to enable students to use text as a data source in the social sciences. Hands-on examples will equip students to work with text data in final projects.
courses.prerequisites_text: POLI/ECON 5D or POLI 30D or POLI 170A or POLI 171 or POLI 172.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Senior Honors Seminar: Frontiers of Political Science
courses.description: This course is open only to seniors interested in qualifying for departmental honors. Admission to the course will be determined by the department. Each student will write an honors essay under the supervision of a member of the faculty.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Research Seminar in Washington, DC
courses.description: (Same as COMM 194, USP 194, HITO 193, SOCI 194, COGS 194) Course attached to six-unit internship taken by students participating in the UCDC Program. Involves weekly seminar meetings with faculty and teaching assistant and a substantial research paper.
courses.prerequisites_text: participating in UCDC Program.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Local Internship in Political Science
courses.description: Individual placements for field learning integrated with political science. A written contract involving all parties with learning objectives, a project outline, and a means of supervision and progress evaluation must be filed with the faculty adviser and department undergraduate coordinator prior to the beginning of the internship. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: ninety units completed; 2.5 minimum cumulative GPA overall and 3.0 in political science; POLI 30 and at least two upper-division courses in political science. Department approval and consent of instructor. Corequisites: POLI 194SD.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the basic concepts in psychology. Topics may include human information processing, learning and memory, motivation, development, language acquisition, social psychology, and personality.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: General Psychology: Biological Foundations
courses.description: This course provides an introductory survey of the relationship between human behavior and brain function. Specific areas of emphasis include vision and other sensory processes, memory, motivation, attention, and cognition.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: General Psychology: Cognitive Foundations
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the basic concepts of cognitive psychology. Topics include perception, attention, memory, language, and thought. The relation of cognitive psychology to cognitive science and to neuropsychology is also covered.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: General Psychology: Social Foundations
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to social psychology. Topics may include emotion, aesthetics, behavioral medicine, person perception, attitudes and attitude change, and behavior in social organizations.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Introduction to Statistics
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to both descriptive and inferential statistics, core tools in the process of scientific discovery and the interpretation of research.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Methods in Psychology
courses.description: This course provides an overview of how to choose appropriate research methods for experimental and nonexperimental studies. Topics may include classic experimental design and counterbalancing, statistical power, and causal inference in experimental and nonexperimental settings.
courses.prerequisites_text: PSYC 60 or equivalent.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Laboratory in Psychological Research Methods
courses.description: This course provides hands-on research experience. Lecture topics will include experimental and nonexperimental designs, research ethics, data analysis, and causal inference. Students will design original research projects, collect and analyze data, and write a full APA-style report, including a brief literature review relevant to their design. This course builds on PSYC 70 by applying design principles to students’ own research questions and ideas. Open to the following Department of Psychology majors only: PC26, PC28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, COGS 14B or PSYC 60 or MATH 11 and PSYC 70 or COGS 14A.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Learning Sustainable Well-Being: Compassion for Self and Others
courses.description: This experiential course teaches the art of practicing psychological well-being based on principles from Eastern and Western philosophies (e.g., mindfulness, positive psychology, cognitive therapy, and neuroscience). Each week, there is a short lecture on a given topic, combined with workshop-style exercises.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study or research under direction of a member of the faculty. May be taken up to three times for a maximum of twelve units.
courses.prerequisites_text: lower-division standing, completion of at least thirty units of undergraduate study at UC San Diego with a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 3.0; completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Clinical Psychology
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the causes, characteristics, and treatment of psychological disorders. Particular emphasis is given to the interaction between biological, psychological, and sociocultural processes contributing to abnormal behavior. Students may not receive credit for both PSYC 163 and PSYC 100.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Developmental Psychology
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the field of developmental psychology, including topics in cognitive, language, and social development.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the field of social psychology, covering a review of the field’s founding principles, classic findings, and a survey of recent findings. Topics will include social perception, attributions and attitudes, stereotypies, social influence, group dynamics, and aggressive and prosocial tendencies.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of cognitive psychology, the scientific study of mental processes: how people acquire, store, transform, use, and communicate information. Topics may include perception, attention, language, memory, reasoning, problem solving, decision-making, and creativity.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Behavioral Neuroscience
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of human and animal behavior from a neuroscience perspective. Topics include the functions and mechanisms of perception, motivation (sex, sleep, hunger, emotions), learning and memory, and motor control and movement.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Cognitive Neuroscience
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of neuroanatomy and major methods and results from neuroimaging and neuropsychological studies of behavior. Topics include attention, motor control, executive function, memory, learning, emotion, and language.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychophysiological Perspectives on the Social Mind Laboratory
courses.description: This course provides an overview and training in the use of psychophysiological methods to investigate the cognitive and emotional process involved in understanding and reacting to other people. Students will develop individual research questions and actively participate in designing and conducting the experiments. Open to the following majors only: PC26, PC28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33, PC34, CG32.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, PSYC 60 or COGS 14B or MATH 11 and PSYC 70 or COGS 14A.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Mechanisms of Animal Behavior
courses.description: This course focuses on approaches to the study of behavior and its underlying fundamental units of analysis in human and nonhuman animals. Students may not receive credit for both PSYC 122 and PSYC 103.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Clinical Assessment and Treatment
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the history, purpose, and recent changes to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders along with appropriate evidence-based interventions. Other topics include psychiatric emergencies, crisis management, and ethics. Recommended preparation: Completion of PSYC 100.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Social Cognition
courses.description: This course provides an overview of social cognition, which blends cognitive and social psychology to understand how people make sense of the social world. Topics may include social perception, inference, memory, motivation, affect, understanding the self, stereotypes, and cultural cognition.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Language
courses.description: This course provides an overview of language comprehension and production. Topics include animal communication, language development, and language disorders. Recommended preparation: completion of a course in language, cognition, or philosophy of the mind.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Behavior Modification
courses.description: The course provides an extension of learning principles to human behavior. Topics include broad implications of a behavioral perspective, applied behavior analysis, and applications of behavioral principles to clinical disorders and to normal behavior in varied settings.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Health Psychology
courses.description: This course provides an exploration of health, illness, and treatment as they relate to psychological concepts and considers how stress influences the body’s physiological systems and risk for physical illnesses.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Science of Imagination
courses.description: This seminar explores how psychologists think about and study the imagination—the capacity to mentally transcend time, place, and circumstance to think about what might have been, plan and anticipate the future, create and become absorbed in fictional worlds, and consider alternatives to actual experiences. You will learn how to evaluate psychological evidence, and how to read, interpret, discuss, present, and write about scientific literature.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. PC25, PC26, PS28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33, PC34, PC35, HS25, HS26, HS27, HS28, HD01, HD02, HD25, HD26, or CG32 major only.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Brain Damage and Mental Function
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the neural mechanisms underlying perception, memory, language, and other mental capacities. Topics include how brain damage affects these capacities and how patients with brain lesions can contribute to our understanding of the normal brain.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Neurobiology of Learning and Memory
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the neurobiology of learning and memory, from cognitive to molecular neuroscience, including human, animal, cellular, and molecular studies of memory. Topics include amnesia, intellectual disability, exceptional intelligence, aging, and Alzheimer’s disease.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and BILD 12 or COGS 107B or COGS 17 or PSYC 106 or PSYC 181 or PSYC 181GS or PSYC 2.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Visual Cognition
courses.description: This course provides an overview of high-level visual perception, and of how visual perception intersects with attention, memory, and concepts. Topics may include an introduction to the visual system with an emphasis on high-level visual regions; object recognition, face recognition, scene recognition and reading; visual attention, including eye movements during scene perception and during reading; and visual working memory.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Industrial Organizational Psychology
courses.description: This course provides an examination of human behavior in industrial, business, and organizational settings. Topics include psychological principles applied to selection, placement, management, and training; the effectiveness of individuals and groups within organizations, including leadership and control; conflict and cooperation; motivation; and organizational structure and design.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychopharmacology—Drugs and Behavior
courses.description: This course provides an overview of basic principles of psychopharmacology, including psychological effects, brain mode of action, and patterns of use of psychoactive agents. Drugs discussed may include drugs of abuse and psychotherapeutics such as stimulants, opioids, sedative hypnotics, hallucinogens, marijuana, alcohol, cognitive enhancers, anxiolytics, antidepressants, and antipsychotics.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Choice and Self-Control
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the experimental analysis of choice behavior, with an emphasis on the types of choice involved in self-control. A central interest will be the conditions under which decision-making is optimal.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Brain, Behavior, and Evolution
courses.description: This course provides a survey of natural behaviors, including birdsong, prey capture, localization, electroreception and echolocation, and the neural system that controls them, emphasizing broad fundamental relationships between brain and behavior across species. Cross-listed with BIPN 189. Students may not receive credit for PSYC 189 and BIPN 189.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, BILD 2 or COGS 101A or COGS 107B or PSYC 102 or PSYC 106.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Topics in Psychology
courses.description: Selected topics in the field of psychology. May be taken for credit three times as topics vary.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology Laboratory Topics
courses.description: Selected laboratory topics in the field of psychology. May be taken for credit two times as topics vary. Open to the following majors only: PC26, PC28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33, PC34, CG32.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, department approval, and PSYC 60 or COGS 14B or MATH 11 and PSYC 70 or COGS 14A.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Honors Thesis I
courses.description: This course provides the opportunity for students to plan and carry out a research project under the guidance of the psychology faculty. Students will write a proposal for the research that they plan to conduct in 194B-C and will present this proposal to the class. Must be taken for a letter grade for the Psychology Honors Program.
courses.prerequisites_text: PSYC 110, PSYC 111A-B, department approval, psychology majors only, acceptance to the Honors Program.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Seminar
courses.description: Weekly research seminar, three quarter research project under faculty guidance which culminates in a thesis. Must be taken for a letter grade to satisfy major requirements for Department of Psychology majors. Open to the following majors only: PC25, PC26, PC28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33, PC34, PC35.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, instructor and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Seminar
courses.description: Weekly research seminar, three quarter research project under faculty guidance which culminates in a thesis. Must be taken for a letter grade to satisfy major requirements for Department of Psychology majors. Open to the following majors only: PC25, PC26, PC28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33, PC34, PC35.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, instructor and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study or laboratory research under direction of faculty in the Department of Psychology. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Statistical Computing and Inference from Data I
courses.description: The first of a series of intensive courses in statistical computing to draw inferences from data. This course covers research design, causal inference, data wrangling, visualization, probability, statistical inference, and the general linear model.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Emotion
courses.description: This seminar provides a selective overview of the scientific study of emotion. We will discuss various theoretical perspectives on emotion and will focus on specific topics such as emotion regulation, affect in social interactions, individual differences, and particular emotions (e.g., embarrassment, envy, and jealousy).
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Area Proseminar in Developmental Psychology
courses.description: The course examines cognitive development through the school-age period and social and personality development from infancy through early adolescence. It begins with an examination of early neurological, sensory, motor, and perceptual functions and then focuses on issues in linguistic and cognitive development. The class will first discuss general developmental theory and methods and then topics such as attachment, temperament, self-concept, aggression, family relations, play, and peers. Students cannot get credit for PSYC 217 if they have already taken PSYC 217A or 217B.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Sensation and Perception
courses.description: Fundamentals of vision, audition, and other senses. Emphasis will be upon psychophysical approaches to the study of these sensory modalities, as well as some essential aspects of their neurophysiological bases.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Cognitive Neural Systems (CNS)
courses.description: A weekly seminar series focused on understanding recent advances in the relationship between neural systems and behavior using a variety of experimental approaches (single unit recording, comp neuro, evolutionary bio, psychophysics, comparative anatomy, lesion work, psychopharm, fMRI, EEG, TMS, etc.). May be taken for credit twenty-four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. S/U grades only.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Tools for Experimental Data Analysis
courses.description: This course will provide an introduction to programming and a set of general data analysis methods that are broadly applicable in many different subdisciplines of psychology/neuroscience. Topics include model fitting, information theory, Fourier analysis, and machine learning. Recommended preparation: Any programming experience will help, but not required. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: PSYC 231, NEUG 231, NEU 231.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Developmental Psychology
courses.description: Advanced seminar concentrating on methods of research and current experimental literature in developmental psychology. May be taken for credit twenty-four times. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Special Topics in Psycholinguistics
courses.description: Discussion of theories and experiments investigating language production, comprehension, or acquisition.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Selected Topics in Cognitive Development
courses.description: An in-depth analysis of selected empirical and theoretical topics in cognitive development. The course will focus on areas where notable progress appears to be taking place in contemporary research.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. Restricted to students with major codes PC81, PC82, PC83, PC84, or consent of the instructor.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Introduction to Laboratory Experimentation I
courses.description: A basic laboratory course designed to introduce first-year graduate students to experimental methods in psychology. The student will select a research topic; do a thorough literature review of the area; design and carry out new, original studies of problems in the selected area; and prepare a final formal report of the study at the end of the spring quarter. This course is required of all first-year graduate students in the department. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Selected Topics in Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: An in-depth analysis of selected empirical and theoretical topics in cognitive psychology. The course will focus on areas where notable progress appears to be taking place in contemporary research.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Social Psychology
courses.description: A biweekly seminar series focusing on recent advances in both basic and applied research in social psychology including topics such as interpersonal relationships, emotion, health, social cognition, judgment, and decision making. May be taken for credit twenty-four times. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: A weekly seminar series focused on understanding recent advances in any area of cognitive psychology. May be taken for credit twenty-four times. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Seminar in Communication and Information Processing
courses.description: S/U grades only.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Practicum
courses.description: Research in psychology under supervision of individual faculty members. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit fifteen times.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Practicum
courses.description: Independent research and thesis research. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit fifteen times.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Apprentice Teaching
courses.description: Teaching practicum for students enrolled in graduate program in psychology. Students who hold appointments as teaching assistants must enroll in this course. Minimum program requirement is for one four-unit course per year for four years. S/U grades only.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Public Health
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the infrastructure of public health; the analytical tools employed by public health practitioners; bio-psychosocial perspectives of public health problems; health promotion/disease prevention; quality assessment in public health; and legal and ethical concerns. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 40. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 40 and PH 40.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Primary Care and Public Health
courses.description: This course explores historical and current interactions, achievements, and challenges of primary care and public health. It will analyze the impact of common medical conditions such as obesity, diabetes, mental health disorders, and others on individuals, their families, and society. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 50. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 50 and PH 50.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Exploring Public Health
courses.description: This seminar-style course offers students the opportunity to explore key areas of public health, covering foundational principles across a variety of topics. Subjects range and may include, but are not limited to, career pathways in public health, strategies for maintaining well-being and academic success, mental health awareness and support, sexual health and reproductive rights, mindfulness practices, financial wellness, stress management, and more.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Selected topics in the field of public health.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Individual undergraduate study or research not covered by the present course offerings. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: completion of thirty units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 3.0, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Epidemiology
courses.description: This course covers the basic principles of epidemiology, with applications to investigations of noninfectious (“chronic”) and infectious diseases. Explores various study designs appropriate for disease surveillance and studies of etiology and prevention. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 101. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 101 and PH 101.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and PSYC 60, HDS 60, MATH 11, or COGS 14B, and upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Biostatistics in Public Health
courses.description: Fundamentals of biostatistics and basic methods for analysis of continuous and binary outcomes for one, two, or several groups. Includes: summarizing and displaying data; probability; statistical distributions; central limit theorem, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing; comparing means of continuous variables between two groups; comparing proportions between two groups; simple and multiple linear regression. Hands-on data analysis using software and statistical applications in public health. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 102. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 102 and PH 102.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and PSYC 60, HDS 60, MATH 11, or COGS 14B, and upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Health Behavior and Chronic Diseases
courses.description: This course introduces health behavior concepts through applications to chronic disease prevention. The focus is on smoking, dietary behaviors, and physical activity and is organized around relationships to health, measurement, influencing factors, interventions, and translation to public health practice. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 110. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 110 and PH 110.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Health Policies for Healthy Lifestyles
courses.description: This course covers the rationale for and effectiveness of policies to influence nutrition, physical activity, and substance use behavior. Policies include legalization, taxation, labeling, produce manufacturing, warning labels, licensing, marketing, and counter-marketing practices and restrictions on use. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 120. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 120 and PH 120.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Environmental and Occupational Health
courses.description: This core public health course addresses the fundamentals of environmental and occupational health, including identification of hazards, basic toxicology, risk assessment, prevention/protection, and regulatory/control policies. Specific environmental and occupational hazards and relevant case studies will be presented. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 130. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 130 and PH 130.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 101 or FMPH 101, and upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Race, Intersectionality, and Public Health
courses.description: This course will explore the intersection of oppressions based on social identities such as race, ethnicity, socioeconomic class, gender, and citizenship status. This course will introduce the framework of intersectionality, with an emphasis on its use within the field of public health and explore and analyze how race and ethnicity are socially constructed and intersect with identities to influence health behavior and outcomes.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and sophomore standing. Renumbered from FMPH 191. Students can’t receive credit for PH 157 if they have already completed FMPH 191 subtitled “Race, Intersectionality, and Public Health.”

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Clinical Nutrition in Public Health
courses.description: Clinical nutrition is the study of nutrition and diet as related to the prevention and treatment of human disease. The practical and psychosocial aspects of diet modification and food/food product availability are key aspects of clinical nutrition practice, whether individual or community based, irrespective of whether the goal is primary prevention or disease treatment. Students will identify applications and translation of nutritional guidelines and recommendations into behavior in the course. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing. Renumbered from FMPH 161. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 161 and PH 161.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Public Health Capstone I
courses.description: This is the first of a two-part capstone series that serves as the culminating experience for the BS in public health (BSPH) majors. Students will integrate the skills and knowledge gained throughout the BSPH program and learn critical elements of public health research and practice. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 45, PH 101 or FMPH 101, PH 102 or FMPH 102, PH 110 or FMPH 110, and PH 120 or FMPH 120. Department approval required. Restricted to senior public health majors only. Renumbered from FMPH 193. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: PH 193, PH 193R, or FMPH 193.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Pedagogy and Learning Apprenticeship
courses.description: Under the supervision of an instructor, undergraduate students gain teaching experience through practical experiences in course management and effective teaching methods. May be taken for credit up to two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: a minimum of A– in the course in which the student plans to assist, a 3.0 cumulative UC GPA, and instructor and department approval.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Investigation of public health topics through directed reading and discussion by a small group of students. Opportunities can also include experiential and research components. Study must be under supervision of a faculty member and approval must be secured from the faculty member prior to registering. P/NP grades only. Renumbered from FMPH 198. PH 198 and/or FMPH 198 may be taken for credit a combined total of nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, completion of ninety units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 2.5, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Individual undergraduate study or research not covered by the present course offerings. Study or research must be under the direction of a faculty member in the Department of Family Medicine and Public Health and approval must be secured from the faculty member prior to registering. P/NP grades only. Renumbered from FMPH 199. PH 199 and/or FMPH 199 may be taken for credit a combined total of nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, completion of ninety units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 2.5, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Mixed Methods Research
courses.description: This course will provide an introduction to the definition, design, and practice of mixed methods research. Mixed methods approaches are becoming increasingly common in many research areas, especially in public health because of the combined use of qualitative and quantitative data sets. This course will teach you to meaningfully integrate the two and takes an applied focus.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: JDP Public Health Seminar
courses.description: This course combines didactic instruction, interactive sessions, and student presentations. Topics cover study design, ethics, data analysis and management techniques, and qualitative research will be presented.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Epidemiology Practicum
courses.description: Students will explore an epidemiologic research question by reviewing relevant published literature, and then design and conduct appropriate data analysis using a preexisting dataset.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: HSRIS Colloquium Series
courses.description: The HSRIS colloquium series is a program of empirical research seminars focused on the most important issues facing patients, providers, health care systems, and policymakers today. It provides an opportunity for HSRIS doctoral students across all stages of completion to meet regularly, analyze and critique ongoing research, and participate in stimulating discussion with HSRIS faculty and guest lecturers.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Practicum in Global Health and Health Behavior
courses.description: Students will learn about grant writing, project management, preparation of manuscripts for publication and presentations for scientific meetings, and also work individually with a faculty mentor in preparing manuscripts using data from a specific health behavior intervention.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Dissemination and Implementation Science in Health: An Introduction
courses.description: This course will emphasize the unique aspects of dissemination and implementation research, including the types of questions it seeks to answer, the outcomes examined and how they differ from other types of studies, the models and frameworks commonly used, and the qualitative and quantitative methods employed.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Dissertation Research in Public Health
courses.description: Public health doctoral program dissertation research units.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Biostatistics
courses.description: Students will understand principles of measurement of clinical data, recognize data types, and determine statistical methods for analysis of a given dataset. They will gain experience in preparing a clinical dataset for analysis. Students will learn basic data visualization, statistical testing and inference, and statistical modeling with R.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 400. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 400 and PH 400.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Epidemiology
courses.description: This course provides a foundational understanding of principles and methods used to study the distribution and determinants of health and disease in populations. Topics include study design, data collection, measures of disease frequency, and risk assessment. Through lectures and small group discussions, students learn to critically evaluate epidemiological research, understand the ethical considerations in conducting epidemiological studies, and recognize common sources of bias and confounding.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 401. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 401 and PH 401.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Health Behavior
courses.description: This course provides an opportunity to explore the theoretical issues and current methodologies related to understanding and influencing health behavior change in diverse populations. The course will focus on the social, behavioral, and biologic determinants of health on the individual, interpersonal, community, institutional, and policy levels. The examples of application of theories to determinants and intervention research and disparities in health behavior and outcomes are covered.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 402. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 402 and PH 402.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Cardiovascular Disease Epidemiology
courses.description: This is an MPH-level course designed to introduce topics in cardiovascular disease epidemiology using the following definition of epidemiology as a guide: Epidemiology is the study of the distribution and determinants of health-related states or events in specified populations, and the application of this study to the control of health problems. As such, the course provides an overview of the prevalence, incidence, and key risk factors for major cardiovascular diseases.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB91) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 401 or PH 401. Students may only receive credit for one of these courses: PH 417, PH 417R, or FMPH 417.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Infectious Disease Epidemic and Economic Modeling for Health Policymaking
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to infectious disease epidemic and cost-effectiveness modeling, with focus on applications to inform health policymaking. This didactic and computer lab-based course will cover basic models for human infectious disease transmission, model parameterization, calibration to surveillance data, projecting the epidemic impact of interventions, and cost-effectiveness modeling of health interventions. Students will learn how to code and analyze models in MATLAB.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB90, and PB91) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 401 or PH 401. Students can’t receive credit for PH 420 if they have already completed FMPH 491 subtitled “Introduction to Infectious Disease Epidemic and Economic Modeling for Health Policymaking.”

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Mental Health Across the Life Course
courses.description: This course examines mental health from infancy through childhood into adulthood and aging. Students will learn how perturbations in mental health manifest differently at different developmental stages over the life course. The course will also cover how early life exposures to stressful circumstances can lead to symptoms, disorder, or disease and how these manifest themselves across development. Students will explore potential strategies for identification of risk, prevention, and intervention.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB89) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 427. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 427 and PH 427.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Substance Use and Population Health
courses.description: This course offers a window into the patterns, drivers, and consequences of substance use from a public health perspective. It also introduces various prevention, treatment, and harm reduction approaches. Through assessment of current epidemiologic data, application of conceptual frameworks, engagement with researchers and practitioners, and reflection on prevention, treatment, and harm reduction policies and strategies, we will explore the complexity of substance use and population health.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, and PB89). Students cannot receive credit for PH 429 if they have already completed FMPH 491 subtitled “Substance Use and Population Health.”

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: The Organization and Financing of the U.S. Health-Care System
courses.description: Students will learn about the organization and financing of health services in the United States and the implications of system characteristics for quality, equity, and health-care costs; develop an understanding of how health policy decisions are made in the United States; and learn how health-care financing in the US compares with other countries around the world. Students will develop the background and skills to solve a range of problems in the fields of health policy and public health.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB88) and successfully completed FMPH 405 or PH 405. Renumbered from FMPH 441. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 441 and PH 441.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Qualitative Research Methods
courses.description: This course introduces master’s students to qualitative research methods, emphasizing the strategies and applications of this methodology in public health, health justice, and community-engaged research. Through lectures, group work, interactive sessions, and practical exercises, students will gain foundational knowledge and skills in qualitative research. Topics also include theoretical foundations of research, biocultural ethics, and the advantages of numerous qualitative inquiry techniques.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB88). Students cannot receive credit for PH 442 if they have already completed FMPH 491 subtitled “Qualitative Research Methods.”

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Current Issues in Public Health
courses.description: Students will be introduced to and discuss important issues in public health in an interactive format with the MPH director, other FMPH faculty, and public health professionals from the San Diego public health community. Each week the class will focus on a different topic and the career path of one or more public health researchers or practitioners.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 461. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 461 and PH 461.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Public Health Leadership in Practice
courses.description: This course is required prior to starting an MPH practicum. This course seeks to expose students to leadership principles and reinforce effective skills necessary at their field site and in their future careers by utilizing a blend of reflective individual and module-based activities to improve written and oral communication skills prior to their practicum. Students will also learn about the various fields and organizations in public health as they explore potential practicum opportunities.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91). Renumbered from FMPH 496A. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 496A and PH 496A.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Public Health Master’s Capstone/Thesis
courses.description: Students complete their capstone/thesis, and potentially submit their capstone/thesis for publication and/or present their capstone/thesis to stakeholders. May be taken for credit up to six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Teaching Methods in Public Health
courses.description: This course is for graduate students wanting to develop skills and knowledge to become a teaching assistant or as preparation for an academic teaching career. The course covers the practice and theory of educating others, curriculum and instructional design, and teaching best practices.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Biostatistical Methods I
courses.description: Introductory graduate course on applied statistical data analysis, focusing on multiple linear regression and using the R statistical software. The course addresses issues related to model interpretation, model assumptions, confounding, interactions, testing of coefficients and ANOVA, adjusting for multiple comparisons, heteroscedasticity, model diagnostics, variable selection, prediction error, cross-validation, and resampling via the bootstrap. Renumbered from FMPH 221. Students may not receive credit for PHB 221 and FMPH 221. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the biostatistics degree requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: biostatistics major or program approval.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Biostatistical Methods in Clinical Trials
courses.description: The graduate-level course will cover statistical aspects of clinical trial design, monitoring, analysis, and ethics of human subjects research. Design and computations will be emphasized. Renumbered from FMPH 224. Students may not receive credit for PHB 224 and FMPH 224. Must be taken for a letter grade if applied to biostatistics degree requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: successful completion of FMPH 221 or PHB 221 and FMPH 222 or PHB 222 and FMPH 223 or PHB 223 or program approval. Restricted to PB76, PB77, PB79, PB80, PB81, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Statistical Learning and Multivariate Analysis
courses.description: This graduate course introduces concepts, methods, and applications of statistical learning and multivariate data analysis, including prediction, classification, regularization, decision trees, principal components analysis, and clustering. Data analysis will be emphasized. Renumbered from FMPH 227. Students may not receive credit for PHB 227 and FMPH 227. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the biostatistics degree requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: successful completion of FMPH 221 or PHB 221 and FMPH 222 or PHB 222 or program approval.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Biostatistics Rotation
courses.description: This practicum provides hand-on experience with biomedical research and data analysis. Working within a specific biomedical domain (e.g., cancer, genomics, or physical activity research), students will conduct original data analysis and prepare or substantially contribute to a final project report. Renumbered from FMPH 241. PHB 241 and/or FMPH 241 may be taken for credit for a combined total of five times.
courses.prerequisites_text: successful completion of FMPH 221 or PHB 221 and FMPH 222 or PHB 222; biostatistics major only.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Practicum in Biostatistics A
courses.description: This is the first in a sequence of two core courses for the MS degree in biostatistics. The course takes advantage of the extensive involvement of the program faculty in collaborative and interdisciplinary work within the life sciences. Didactic instruction on best practices in statistical collaboration. Under supervision, the students will participate in applied, real-life projects stemming from the research and collaborations of the faculty in the Division of Biostatistics. Renumbered from FMPH 243A. Students may not receive credit for PHB 243A and FMPH 243A.
courses.prerequisites_text: successful completion of FMPH 221 or PHB 222 and FMPH 223 or PHB 223. Restricted to major code PB76.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Foundations in Biostatistics A
courses.description: This course will mainly focus on probability theory and mathematical statistics, which are essential building blocks for more advanced inference tools. Topics include probability theory, (multivariate) random variables, functions of random variables, expectations, variance and moments, common families of distributions, properties of a random sample, statistics and sampling distribution, convergence of a sequence of random variables. Renumbered from FMPH 244A. Students may not receive credit for PHB 244A and FMPH 244A. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the biostatistics degree requirements. Restricted to major code PB76.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Biostatistics Journal Club
courses.description: This is a biweekly, structured journal club. Students will critically read assigned articles. During meetings, students work in groups to discuss specific questions regarding the assigned article, and are asked to present their answers to the class. Renumbered from FMPH 290. PHB 280 and/or FMPH 290 may be taken for credit for a combined total of six times. Restricted to major codes PB76 or PB77.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Biostatistics Seminar Series
courses.description: Through a combination of in-person and virtual seminars on Zoom, students will gain insight into current research projects presented by invited speakers. Additionally, students are provided with the opportunity to participate in lunch discussions and one-on-one meetings. All MS students in biostatistics, and biostatistics PhD students in their third year and above are highly encouraged to enroll quarterly (except for summer). May be taken for credit up to twelve times.
courses.prerequisites_text: FMPH 290 or PHB 280. Restricted to PB76 and PB77 majors.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Independent study for biostatistics graduate students in the Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science. Study of special topics for graduate students under the direction of a faculty member. Exact subject matter to be arranged in individual cases. Restricted to PB76 and PB77 majors. May be taken for credit up to twenty-one times.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval required.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Dissertation Research
courses.description: Dissertation research for students who are advancing or have advanced to candidacy. May be taken for credit up to twelve times. Renumbered from FMPH 299. PHB 299 and/or FMPH 299 may be taken for credit for a combined total of twelve times.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval required.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Financial Accounting
courses.description: Overview of financial accounting reporting, with a primary focus on the analysis of economic events and their effect on the major financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, and statement of cash flows). Learn the nature and purpose of accounting methods. Letter grades only. Students may receive credit for one of the following: MGTF 401, MGT 404, or MGT 404R.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Investment Analysis
courses.description: Introduces quantitative methods for analyzing the pricing and return behavior of assets such as stocks, bonds, and derivatives; and develops methods for implementing modern portfolio theory in practice. The most influential financial models are derived; their practical applications are discussed. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Financial Econometrics and Empirical Methods
courses.description: Bridging the gap between theoretical financial models and the real world. Covering the major accomplishments of empirical finance. Empirical exercises and analysis of real financial data will help students to truly appreciate the content of the course. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Business Forecasting
courses.description: Introduction to state-of-the-art forecasting methods in finance. Students will learn to estimate forecasting models based on past values of the predicted variable(s), surveys, market information, and other economic data. Participants will become critical consumers of forecasts reported in the media. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Collecting and Analyzing Financial Data
courses.description: Teaches students how to obtain and process data in order to answer empirical questions in finance. The data can be numerical or textual, and structured or unstructured. Specific data sources may include CRSP, Compustat, Thomson Reuters, and Bloomberg. Some programming. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Preparing for the CFA Exam
courses.description: The Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) designation is the industry-accepted gold standard for financial analysts. To earn the CFA charter, students must pass three very challenging exams. Students will look at each of the ten major topic areas and explore the level of understanding that is required to pass the first-level exam. Students will do applied valuation work as well as highlight study habits of successful past candidates.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Capstone: Applied Finance Project
courses.description: The Capstone project is one of the primary measures of student learning. Evaluation is based on students’ ability to apply course material to the Capstone project. Satisfactory completion of the project is required for award of the degree. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGTF 402, MGTF 403, MGTF 404, and restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Special Topics in Finance
courses.description: Introduces advanced topics of special interest in finance. Instructional methods can include face-to-face lecture, case presentations, assigned teaching, and/or online group discussions. May be taken for credit up to four times. Students may not earn credit when course subtitles are the same.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Quantitative Methods in Business
courses.description: Introduction to techniques to develop/analyze data for informed tactical and strategic management decisions: statistical inference, probability, regression analysis, and optimization. Using these analytic approaches, theory-based formulas, and spreadsheets, students explore managerial applications across all areas of business activity.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Financial Accounting
courses.description: Cross-listed with ECON 4. Recording, organizing, and communicating financial information to business entities.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Managerial Accounting
courses.description: Internal accounting fundamentals, including cost behavior, cost application methods, overhead allocation methods, break-even analysis, budgeting, cost variance analysis, inventory management, and capital budgeting.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Personal Financial Management
courses.description: Course examines management of personal financial assets: savings and checking accounts, fixed assets, and credit cards. Budgeting, loan applications, payment terms, and statement reconciliation will be covered as will credit ratings, cash management, compound interest, bank operations, and contract obligations.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Personal Ethics at Work
courses.description: Course examines the ethical foundation for choices individuals make every day both in the workplace and in their private lives, the connection between economic and ethical obligations with examples related to privacy, reporting, whistle-blowing, workplace relationships, confidentiality, and intellectual property.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Managing Diverse Teams
courses.description: The modern workplace includes people different in culture, gender, age, language, religion, education, and more. Students will learn why diverse teams make better decisions and are often integral to the success of organizations. Topics include challenges of diversity, and the impact of emotional, social, and cultural intelligence on team success. Content will include significant attention to the experiences of Asian Americans and African Americans as members and leaders of such diverse teams. Students will not receive credit for both MGT 18 and MGT 18GS.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Principles of Accounting
courses.description: Covers the principles, methods and applications of general accounting, cost accounting and investment ROI. Development of the three key financial reports and their interrelations, cost identification, product costing, inventory control, operational performance, and investment return

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Test and Measurement in the Workplace
courses.description: This course introduces students to the psychometric, legal, ethical, and practical considerations of using tests and measurements for evidence-based decision-making in the workplace. Emphasis is given to selection and performance measurements for individual, team, business unit and organization-wide use in marketing, STEM, and operations. Student teams will develop managerial recommendations following company specific research and analysis.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Operating a Successful Business
courses.description: Operating a business is a complex task but a skill that can be mastered. Business managers make interconnected decisions to bring products and services to market. How many workers should a burrito chain employ given demand projections and which burrito-building tasks should be completed before a customer walks in? When a bakery makes pastries, how many at a time? Why do airlines overbook? Managers must answer these questions to keep operations lean and outdo competitors. Students will not receive credit for both MGT 71 and MGT 71R.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Customer Analytics
courses.description: Marketers use empirical models to determine, support, and evaluate a wide range of business decisions. This course covers models and estimation techniques commonly used for understanding segmentation, targeting, and positioning; product diffusion; advertising response, among other topics. Recommended preparation: ECON 120A. Familiarity with R will be assumed.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and BENG 100 or COGS 14B or ECE 109 or ECON 120A or MAE 108 or MATH 11 or MATH 180A or MATH 183 or MATH 186 or MGT 3 or PSYC 60 or SIO 187.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Product Marketing and Management
courses.description: Defining markets for products and services, segmenting these markets, and targeting critical customers within segments. Strategies to position products and services within segments. The critical role of pricing as well as market research, product management, promotion, selling, and customer support.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Product Promotion and Brand Management
courses.description: Principles and decisions to be considered in overall communications and promotion strategy for traditional channels and emerging social networks. Decisions on promotional mix, ad design, implementation and evaluation for establishing brand equity, measure brand performance and sustaining brand equity.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGT 100 or MGT 103.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Applied Market Research
courses.description: The business world revolves around managerial decisions, and those ought to be data driven. In this course we will learn about planning, implementing, and analyzing market research; synthesizing multi-methods research; and presenting market research results by actually doing it. We will learn how to plan and conduct interviews; how to design, execute, and analyze surveys; and how to employ cutting-edge tools such as adaptive conjoint analysis to quantify attribute levels and trade-offs. This course is a distance education course.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Topics in Marketing
courses.description: Introduces advanced topics of special interest in marketing. Topics may include advertising, consumer behavior, pricing, product life cycles, etc. This course may also cover the unique demands of innovation-driven, biotech, and high-technology markets. May be taken for credit no more than three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGT 100 or MGT 103, upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Global Business Strategy
courses.description: Will examine the advantages and complications of the multinational organization with emphasis on translating marketing, financing, and operating plans in light of geographical, cultural, and legal differences across the globe. Will also cover organizational considerations for transglobal management.
