courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 129 and SOCC 129.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Medical Sociology
courses.description: An inquiry into the roles of culture and social structure in mediating the health and illness experiences of individuals and groups. Topics include the social construction of illness, the relationships between patients and health professionals, and the organization of medical work.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 135 and SOCC 135.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Sociology of Mental Illness in Contemporary Society
courses.description: This course will focus on recent developments in the mental illness sector and on the contemporary sociological literature on mental illness. Developments in England as well as the United States will be examined.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 136F and SOCC 136B.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Sociology of Food
courses.description: Topics include food as a marker of social differences (e.g., gender, class, ethnicity); the changing character of food production and distribution; food as an object of political conflict; and the symbolic meanings and rituals of food preparation and consumption.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 137 and SOCB 137.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Genetics and Society
courses.description: The class will first examine the direct social effects of the “genetic revolution”: eugenics, genetic discrimination, and stratification. Second, the implications of thinking of society in terms of genetics, specifically—sociobiology, social Darwinism, evolutionary psychology, and biology.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 138 and SOCC 138 or SOCI 138 and SOCI 138GS.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Sociology of Law
courses.description: This course analyzes the functions of law in society, the social sources of legal change, social conditions affecting the administration of justice, and the role of social science in jurisprudence.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 140 and SOCC 140.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Law and Society in China
courses.description: This course offers an overview of the courts of China. The focus is not on blackletter law. Instead, we look at what grassroots courts do on a daily basis. China has arguably the largest court system in the world. What does it do? How are the courts organized internally? What is the relationship between the courts and other government bureaucracies? Is there the rule of law in China? The course will address these questions by reviewing latest empirical research on the subject area.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Social Deviance
courses.description: This course studies the major forms of behavior seen as rule violations by large segments of our society and analyzes the major theories trying to explain them, as well as processes of rulemaking, rule enforcing, techniques of neutralization, stigmatization and status degradation, and rule change.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 142 and SOCB 142.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Love
courses.description: This course examines the complex historical, cultural, and social psychological landscape surrounding the concept of romantic (as opposed to platonic or familial) love, culminating with a critical analysis of the changing nature of intimate relationships in modern American society. Accordingly, this course will address concepts and insights at the intersection of many subfields: culture, gender, sexuality, family, social networks, social psychology, and computer-mediated communication.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Political Sociology
courses.description: Course focuses on the interaction between state and society. It discusses central concepts of political sociology (social cleavages, mobilization, the state, legitimacy), institutional characteristics, causes, and consequences of contemporary political regimes (liberal democracies, authoritarianism, communism), and processes of political change.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 148 and SOCC 148.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Inequality and Jobs
courses.description: Some people do much better than others in the world of work. Causes and consequences of this inequality will be examined: How do characteristics of individuals (e.g., class, gender, race, education, talent) and characteristics of jobs affect market outcomes?
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 148E and SOCC 148L.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Madness and the Movies
courses.description: Hollywood has had an ongoing obsession with mental illness. This course will examine a number of important or iconic films on this subject. By examining them against a background provided by relevant scholarly materials, we shall develop a critical perspective on these cultural artifacts.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 150 and SOCC 150.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Urban Sociology
courses.description: (Same as USP 105.) Introduces students to the major approaches in the sociological study of cities and to what a sociological analysis can add to our understanding of urban processes.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor. Will not receive credit for SOCI 153 and SOCC 153.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Sociology of Knowledge
courses.description: This course provides a general introduction to the development of the sociology of knowledge and will explore questions concerning social determination of consciousness as well as theoretical ways to articulate a critique of ideology.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 166 and SOCB 166.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Shifting Ideologies of Gender and Sexuality in Science
courses.description: Explore how contemporary understandings of gender and sexuality have been influenced by research in science and medicine and how preconceptions about gender and sexuality influence research. How are discrepancies between what scientists assume about gender and sexual difference reconciled with evidence to the contrary? How have ideas changed over time? Topics range from sex differences in health outcomes, intersexuality, neuroplasticity, environmental exposure, and sports medicine.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Films and Society
courses.description: An analysis of films and how they portray various aspects of American society and culture.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 172 and SOCB 172.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Sociology of Health, Illness, and Medicine
courses.description: This course will explore the social forces that shape our health and the way we understand illness. Themes will include American public health and health care, inequality and biomedicine, as well as special topics like suicide, lead, autism, and HIV/AIDS.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Social Movements and Social Protest
courses.description: An examination of the nature of protests and violence, particularly as they occur in the context of larger social movements. The course will further examine those generic facets of social movements having to do with their genesis, characteristic forms of development, relationship to established political configurations, and gradual fading away.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 180 and SOCC 180.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Gender and Film
courses.description: This class will examine issues of masculinity and femininity through analysis of films. Emphasis is on contemporary American society and will include varying issues such as race, class, and sexualities; worlds of work; romance, marriage, and family.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 184 and SOCC 184.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Honors Seminar: Advanced Studies in Sociology
courses.description: This seminar will permit honors students to explore advanced issues in the field of sociology. It will also provide honors students the opportunity to develop a senior thesis proposal on a topic of their choice and begin preliminary work on the honors thesis under faculty supervision.
courses.prerequisites_text: acceptance into Department of Sociology Honors Program.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Introduction to Structures and Design
courses.description: Introduction to fundamentals of structures and how structures work. Overview of structural behavior and structural design process through hands-on projects. Lessons learned from structural failures. Professional ethics. Role and responsibility of structural engineers. Introduction to four structural engineering focus sequences. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: none. Enrollment restricted to SE27, SE28, SE29, SE30, and SE31 majors only.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study or research under direction of a faculty member.
courses.prerequisites_text: student must be of first year standing and a Regents Scholar. Consent of instructor or department stamp.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Mechanics I: Statics
courses.description: Statics of particles and rigid bodies in two and three dimensions using vector representation; free body diagrams; analysis of trusses, frames, and machines; internal forces; shear force and bending moment diagrams; equilibrium problems with friction; introduction to moment of inertia.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20C or MATH 31BH and PHYS 2A or PHYS 2AR.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Mechanics III: Vibrations
courses.description: Free and forced vibrations of damped 1-DOF systems; vibrations isolation, impact and packaging problems. Analysis of discrete MDOF systems using matrix representation; normal mode of frequencies and modal matrix formulation. Lagrange’s equations. Modal superposition for analysis of continuous vibrating systems.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 18 or MATH 31AH and SE 101B.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Structural Materials
courses.description: This course will provide lectures and labs on the structural properties of engineering materials. Topics covered will include stress and strain, strain measurement, stiffness, strength, toughness, fatigue resistance, and creep. The course will also cover different materials such as cement and concrete, woods, aluminum alloys, steel, engineering plastics, and composite materials. Corequisite: SE 110A.
courses.prerequisites_text: SE 1 and SE 101A.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Statistics, Probability and Reliability
courses.description: Probability theory. Statistics, data analysis and inferential statistics, distributions, confidence intervals. Introduction to structural reliability and random phenomena. Applications to components and systems. Students will not receive credit for both SE 125 and MAE 108.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 18 or MATH 31AH and MATH 20D. Enrollment restricted to SE27, SE28, SE29, SE30, and SE31 majors only.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Structural Analysis I
courses.description: Classical methods of analysis for statically indeterminate structures. Development of computer codes for the analysis of civil, mechanical, and aerospace structures from the matrix formulation of the classical structural theory, through the direct stiffness formulation, to production-type structural analysis programs.
courses.prerequisites_text: grade of C– or better in SE 110A.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Finite Element Analysis: Beam and Shell Models
courses.description: Project-based exploration of structural engineering computations. Topics include analysis of shell structures, design optimization, computational vibration analysis.
courses.prerequisites_text: SE 131A, SE 101C, and SE 130B.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Mechanics and Design of Composite Structures
courses.description: Introduction to advanced composite materials and their applications. Fiber and matrix properties, micromechanics, stiffness, ply-by-ply stress, hygrothermal behavior, and failure prediction. Lab activity will involve design, analysis, fabrication, and testing of composite structure. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: SE 110A or MAE 131A or MAE 131AR and SE 110B or MAE 131.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Nondestructive Evaluation
courses.description: Fourier signal processing, liquid penetrant, elastic wave propagation, ultrasonic testing, impact-echo, acoustic emission testing, vibrational testing, infrared thermography. May be coscheduled with SE 263.
courses.prerequisites_text: SE 110A.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Earthquake Engineering
courses.description: Dynamic analysis of structures due to seismic ground motions. Seismic hazard, earthquake magnitude, and intensity scales. Elements of seismology. Elastic and inelastic response spectra. Modal analysis, linear and nonlinear time-history analysis. Earthquake resistant design. Seismic codes. Elements of geotechnical earthquake engineering.
courses.prerequisites_text: grade of C– or better in all SE 9, SE 101C, and SE 110A. Enrollment restricted to SE27, SE28, SE29, SE30, SE31 majors only.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Geotechnical Engineering
courses.description: General introduction to physical and engineering properties of soils. Soil classification and identification methods. Compaction and construction control. Total and effective stress. Permeability, seepage, and consolidation phenomena. Shear strength of sand and clay.
courses.prerequisites_text: grade of C– or better in SE 110A. Enrollment restricted to SE27, SE28, SE29, SE30, SE31 majors only.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent reading or research on a problem by special arrangement with a faculty member. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor or department stamp.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Advanced Structural Analysis
courses.description: Application of advanced analytical concepts to structural engineering problems. Analysis of frame structures using matrix methods and introduction to the finite element method. Displacement-based and force-based beam element formulations. Development of computer programs for structural analysis. Use of computer resources.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Structural Dynamics I
courses.description: Response of discrete linear structural systems to harmonic, periodic and transient excitations. Lagrangian mechanics. Linearization of the equations of motion. Free and forced vibrations of multi degree-of-freedom structures. Normal mode, frequency response and numerical methods. Continuous systems.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Advanced Structural Steel Design
courses.description: Load and Resistance Factor Design (LRFD) philosophy. Behavior and design of steel elements for global and local buckling. Background of seismic codes. Ductility requirements and capability design concept. Seismic design of steel moment frames and braced frames. Recommended preparation: SE 130A and SE 150A, or equivalent course, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Seismic Isolation and Energy Dissipation
courses.description: Concepts, advantages, and limitations of seismic isolation techniques; fundamentals of dynamic response under seismic excitation; spectral analysis; damping; energy approach; application to buildings and structures.
courses.prerequisites_text: SE 221 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Advanced Seismic Design of Structures
courses.description: Modal analysis. Nonlinear response spectra. Performance based seismic design. Nonlinear time history analyses. Capacity design. Structural walls. Coupled walls. Rocking walls. Base isolation. Recommended preparation: grade of B+ or higher in SE 211 and SE 201B.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval and graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Computational Techniques in Finite Elements
courses.description: Cross-listed with MAE 235. Practical application of the finite element method to problems in solid mechanics. Elements of theory are presented as needed. Covered are static and dynamic heat transfer and stress analysis. Basic processing, solution methods, and postprocessing are practiced with commercial finite element software. Students may not receive credit for SE 233 and MAE 235.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Advanced Soil Mechanics
courses.description: Advanced treatment of topics in soil mechanics, including state of stress, pore pressure, consolidation and settlement analysis, shear strength of cohesionless and cohesive soils, mechanisms of ground improvement, and slope stability analysis. Concepts in course reinforced by laboratory experiments.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Numerical Methods in Geomechanics
courses.description: Application of finite element method to static and dynamic analysis of geotechnical structures. One-, 2-, and 3-D static and seismic response of earth structures/slopes/Foundation systems. Pore-pressure generation/effects during cycle loading. System identification using strong motion downhole-array data. Use of computer resources required.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Engineering Properties of Soils
courses.description: Experimental/constitutive modeling perspectives on mechanical, hydraulic, thermal behavior of dry and saturated soils. Experimental techniques and methodologies presented; students will be able to perform key tests. Behavior of saturated sands and clays described based on key studies. Calibration of constitutive models for stress-strain behavior of soils, including hyperbolic, Mohr-Coulomb/Cam-Clay models. Modification of these models to consider thermal effects.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Mechanics and Design of Composite Structures
courses.description: Graduate-level introduction to advanced composite materials and their applications. Fiber and matrix properties, 3D properties, stress-strain relationships, micromechanics, stiffness, ply-by-ply stress, classical laminated plate theory, hygrothermal/CTE behavior, and failure prediction. Lab activity will involve composite fabrication methods and design, analysis, build, and testing of composite structure. May be coscheduled with SE 142. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Nondestructive Evaluation
courses.description: Fourier signal processing, liquid penetrant, elastic wave propagation, ultrasonic testing, impact-echo, acoustic emission testing, vibrational testing, infrared thermography. May be coscheduled with SE 163. Recommended Preparation: undergraduate degree in structural, civil, mechanical, or aerospace engineering.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Solid Mechanics for Structural and Aerospace Engineering
courses.description: Application of principles of solid mechanics to structural components and systems, description of stresses, strains, and deformation. Use of conservation equations and principle of minimum potential energy. Development of constitutive equations for metallic cementitious and polymeric materials.
courses.prerequisites_text: SE 110A or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Finite Element Methods in Solid Mechanics I
courses.description: Finite element methods for linear problems in solid mechanics. Emphasis on the principle of virtual work, finite element stiffness matrices, various finite element formulations and their accuracy and the numerical implementation required to solve problems in small strain, isotropic elasticity in solid mechanics.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Structural Optimization
courses.description: Construction of structural design as an optimization problem; mathematical programming for sizing, shape, and topology; linear and nonlinear programming; continuous and discrete optimization methods; Lagrangian function and KKT optimality condition; MATLAB. Use of computer resources.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Design Optimization for Additive Manufacturing
courses.description: This course will cover the following topics: fundamental mathematical concepts of optimization, constrained optimization, sensitivity analysis, topology optimization methods (SIMP and Level Set Topology Optimization), state of the art topology optimization applications and additive manufacturing methods, and future perspectives.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Structural Engineering Seminar
courses.description: Weekly seminar and discussion by faculty, visitors, postdoctoral research fellows and graduate students concerning research topics in earthquake engineering and related subjects. May be repeated for credit. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Graduate Research
courses.description: (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Teaching Experience
courses.description: Teaching experience in an appropriate SE undergraduate course under direction of the faculty member in charge of the course. Lecturing one hour per week in either a problem-solving section or regular lecture.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and the department. (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: SYN
courses.title: Inquiring about a Changing Planet
courses.description: Synthesis 2 builds upon the skills developed in Synthesis 1. In the first half of the quarter, students learn the links between climate change and racial justice. Using an antiracist framework, students work in a small group to research an aspect of the climate crisis. In the second half of the quarter, students are introduced to project design and learn how to draft a proposal. Students learn how to determine the scope of a project based on such criteria as time, money, and potential impact.
courses.prerequisites_text: Seventh College students only, SYN 1/1R, must be taken for a letter grade to count toward Seventh College general-education requirements. Duplicate credit with SYN 2R.

courses.subject: SYN
courses.title: Inquiring about a Changing Planet
courses.description: Synthesis 2R builds upon the skills developed in Synthesis 1. In the first half of the quarter, students learn the links between climate change and racial justice. Using an antiracist framework, students work in a small group to research an aspect of the climate crisis. In the second half of the quarter, students are introduced to project design and learn how to draft a proposal. Students learn how to determine the scope of a project based on such criteria as time, money, and potential impact.
courses.prerequisites_text: Seventh College students only, SYN 1/1R, must be taken for a letter grade to count toward Seventh College general-education requirements. Duplicate credit with SYN 2.

courses.subject: SYN
courses.title: Engaging with a Changing Planet
courses.description: SYN 100 is a project-based course that builds upon foundational skills by taking a collaborative, interdisciplinary approach to complex global problems. Each section focuses on a different theme, challenge, or question related to the climate crisis. Despite the different class topics, all students will learn by designing and executing a team project that addresses their section’s theme.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to Seventh College students only, upper-division standing, completion of SYN 1/1R and SYN 2/2R, must be taken for a letter grade to count toward Seventh College general-education requirements.

courses.subject: SYN
courses.title: Defining the Scope of a Changing Planet
courses.description: SYN 150 is recommended for Seventh College transfer students in preparation for SYN 100. Students critically examine, through an interdisciplinary and antiracist lens, key issues impacting our changing planet.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to Seventh College transfer students only, must be taken for a letter grade to count toward Seventh College high-impact requirement, cannot be taken concurrently or after SYN 100. Duplicate credit with SYN 150R.

courses.subject: SYN
courses.title: Defining the Scope of a Changing Planet
courses.description: SYN 150R is recommended for Seventh College transfer students in preparation for SYN 100. Students critically examine, through an interdisciplinary and antiracist lens, key issues impacting our changing planet.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to Seventh College transfer students only, must be taken for a letter grade to count toward Seventh College high-impact requirement, cannot be taken concurrently or after SYN 100. Duplicate credit with SYN 150.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Introduction to Acting
courses.description: A beginning course in the fundamentals of acting: establishing a working vocabulary and acquiring the basic skills of the acting process. Through exercises, compositions, and improvisations, the student actor explores the imagination as the actor’s primary resource, and the basic approach to text through action.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Acting I
courses.description: This course focuses on beginning scene study with an emphasis on exploring action/objective and the given circumstances of a selected text.
courses.prerequisites_text: THAC or TDAC 1 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Acting II
courses.description: Further study in the application of the given circumstances to a text and the development of characterization.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDAC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Classical Text
courses.description: Studies in the heightened realities of poetic drama. Verse analysis, research, methods and how to approach a classical dialogue.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDAC 102.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Improvisation for the Theatre
courses.description: Improvisation for the Theatre explores improvisation techniques as an alternative and unique approach to acting. Students should have a performance background.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDAC 1.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Advanced Topics
courses.description: Advanced topics in acting, such as avant-garde drama, commedia, or Beckett, for students who possess basic acting techniques. May be taken for credit four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDAC 102.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Movement for Actors
courses.description: An exploration of the wide array of physical skills necessary for the actor. Using techniques derived from mime, clowning, sports, acrobatics, and improvisation, students will investigate their individual physical potential as well as their sense of creativity and imagination.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDAC 101.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Ensemble: Undergraduate Production
courses.description: Participation in a fully staged theatre production directed by an MFA or PhD student for the Department of Theatre and Dance. Admission by audition only.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of the instructor; department stamp.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Advanced Studies in Performance
courses.description: Participation in a fully staged season production that is directed by a faculty member or guest for the Department of Theatre and Dance. Admission by audition only.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of the instructor; department stamp.

courses.subject: TDDE
courses.title: Introduction to Design for the Theatre
courses.description: A survey of contemporary and historical concepts and practices in the visual arts of the theatre; studies in text analysis, studio processes and technical production; elementary work in design criticism, scale model making, and costume design. A course serving as an introduction to theatre design and production.

courses.subject: TDDE
courses.title: Assistant Designer
courses.description: A production-oriented course that continues to introduce students to the fundamentals of design assisting. Laboratory format allows the student to work with faculty, graduate, or advanced undergraduate theatre designers, doing research, developing design concepts, and supporting the designer in a number of professional ways. May be taken for credit up to six times for a maximum of twelve units. A maximum of eight total units may be used towards major requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDDE 1; consent of instructor and department approval required.

courses.subject: TDDE
courses.title: Special Topics in Theatre Design
courses.description: A course designed to expose the theatre design students to a variety of specialized topics that will vary from quarter to quarter. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDDE 1 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDDE
courses.title: Undergraduate Main Stage Production: Design
courses.description: A course that will guide a student in a design assignment on the undergraduate main stage production. Specialized topics dependent on the design requirements of the production. Students may repeat this course a maximum of six times or can receive up to twelve units, whichever is met first. A maximum of eight total units may be used towards major requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDDE 1 and TDDE 101 or TDDE 111 or TDDE 121 or TDDE 131, or consent of instructor. Instructor and department approval required.

courses.subject: TDDE
courses.title: Theatre Process—Sound Design
courses.description: A hands-on course on the process of sound design from conception to planning and implementation. The course will concentrate equally on the technical and artistic aspects of the sound design process and will include a survey of modern audio technologies.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDPR 6 or TDDE 1 or MUS 173 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDDR
courses.title: Stage Management
courses.description: Discussion and research into the duties, responsibilities, and roles of a stage manager. Work to include studies in script analysis, communication, rehearsal procedures, performance skills, and style and conceptual approach to theatre. THGE or TDGE 1, THAC or TDAC 1, and THDE or TDDE 1 recommended.

courses.subject: TDDR
courses.title: Advanced Stage Management
courses.description: This course is a further exploration of theory as a guide to practice in the field of stage management and other leadership roles. This class will delve more deeply into many of the topics that are covered in TDDR 101 and will encourage the development of numerous hard and soft skills that are necessary to become a successful stage manager.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDDR 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDDR
courses.title: Directing-Acting Process
courses.description: A studio class that investigates the fundamental skills a director needs to work with actors. Working with actors, students learn how to animate the text onstage through status exercises and scene work as they develop their skill in text work, staging, and dramatic storytelling.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDDR 108 or TDHT 10, upper-division standing or consent of instructor. Restricted to students within the TH26 major. All other students will be allowed as space permits.

courses.subject: TDDR
courses.title: Major Project in Directing
courses.description: For the advanced student in directing. Intensive concentration on the full realization of a dramatic text from research and analysis through rehearsal and into performance. A maximum of eight units of major project study, regardless of area (design, directing, or stage management) may be used to fulfill major requirements. See department for application. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDDR 108, TDDR 111, consent of instructor, and department stamp.

courses.subject: TDGE
courses.title: Introduction to Theatre
courses.description: An introduction to fundamental concepts in drama and performance. Students will attend performances and learn about how the theatre functions as an art and as an industry in today’s world.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: TDGE
courses.title: Theatre and Film
courses.description: Theatre and Film analyzes the essential differences between theatrical and cinematic approaches to drama. Through selected play/film combinations, the course looks at how the director uses actors and the visual languages of the stage and screen to guide and stimulate the audience’s responses.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: TDGE
courses.title: Great Performances on Film
courses.description: Course examines major accomplishments in screen acting from the work of actors in films or in film genres. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: TDGE
courses.title: Public Speaking
courses.description: This course is designed to establish a clear understanding of the fundamentals of effective oral communication. The methodologies explore the integration of relaxation, concentration, organization, and clear voice and diction as applied to various public speaking modes.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: TDGE
courses.title: Cult Films: Weirdly Dramatic
courses.description: A select survey of eight to ten exceptional offbeat, frequently low-budget films from the last sixty years that have attained cult status. The mix includes Tod Browning’s Freaks (1932) to John Water’s Pink Flamingos (1973). Aspects of bad taste, cinematic irony, and theatrical invention will be highlighted.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGE
courses.title: Visual Ideas
courses.description: An exploration of fundamental ways of seeing and thinking about the performance space. A look at the design process as it reflects styles and attitudes through an examination of text/image/meaning/message in theatre, dance, opera, and visual arts. With a special emphasis on the “solution-finding process” in design, as a leap from text to context, to finalized design.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGE
courses.title: Special Projects
courses.description: Qualified students will pursue a special project in theatre history, problems of production and performance, and similarly appropriate topics.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, 2.5 GPA, consent of instructor, and department stamp.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Stage Combat
courses.description: A study of the dramatic elements of stage violence, and practical work in developing the physical skills necessary to fully realize violent moments on the stage. At the core of the study is the process from text to convincing theatrical action. Physical work revolves around basic principles of energy, focus, and center inherent in unarmed and weapons combat.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Process I—Part I
courses.description: The actors focus on the nature of the acting process, using various exercises to stimulate imagination and to inspire instinctual choices. Later work includes improvisational and imaginative experiences to explore character and text. The class culminates in intensive scene work chosen for the particular actor to meld the improvisational approach with scripted material. The class is a combination of both actors and directors so that a common language is developed.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Acting Practicum
courses.description: One-on-one laboratory workshop that examines practical applications of accents, speech and voice work, dialect, movement and combat work specific and ancillary to the productions in which the students have been cast.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Movement for Theatre I
courses.description: An intensive studio course in the art of movement as a basis for theatre performance. Theory and practice of energy flow, weight, spatial focus, time consumption, and the shape factor. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: THGR or TDGR 213A for B, THGR or TDGR 213B for C; admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Voice for Theatre I—Part I
courses.description: Voice exercises designed to “free the voice” with emphasis on diaphragmatic breathing, articulation exercises, and singing exercises. Course designed to broaden pitch, range, projection, and to expand the full range of potential characterizations.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Directing Process Studio
courses.description: Preparation, presentation, and discussion of representative scenes from various periods of dramatic literature.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Theatre Externship
courses.description: Selected professional opportunities in repertory and commercial theatre, designed to engage the student in particular creative responsibilities under the guidance of master artist-teachers. Student is expected to give biweekly reports detailing his/her experience with the professional company.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Professional Preparation for the Actor
courses.description: A twice-weekly seminar focusing on the actor’s confrontation with the industry, including in-depth preparation for auditions; cold readings; and meetings/interviews with producers, casting directors, agents, and managers. Actors will also begin to create material that could be crafted into solo performances.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Acting for the Camera
courses.description: This course is designed to aid the actor in the transition from stage to film work. Examination of film production and its physical characteristics and the acting style needed for work in film and television. Students will rehearse and perform in simulated studio setting.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Singing for the Actor III
courses.description: Continuing vocal technique for the musical theatre. More complicated musical material investigated and prepared.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Skills
courses.description: A unifying approach to acting skills (voice, movement, and speech) designed to result in providing the graduating actor with a daily regimen appropriate for professional work.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Directing Seminar
courses.description: A seminar focusing on the current directing projects of all graduate directing students. Depending upon individual student needs, the work may include play selection, historical or sociological research, and discussion of emerging directorial concepts, the rehearsal process, and postproduction evaluation.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: New Plays Workshop
courses.description: A course where playwrights and actors work together to develop new plays-in-progress.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Directing Practicum
courses.description: Students enrolled in this course will work on productions in the function of a director. This will include staging, creative interpretation, blocking, etc.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Playwriting Seminar
courses.description: A seminar focusing on the current playwriting project of all graduate playwriting students. Work for each quarter is individually determined according to student needs, but may include exploration of an inceptive idea, development of a scenario or other structural work, and writing dialogue. Students present work to be discussed in class. May include group or individual playwriting exercises.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Playwriting Practicum
courses.description: Creative writing project developing original scripts from outline to the final play. Plays may vary depending on the quarter but will include writing of a realistic one-act, a nonrealistic one-act, a one-act documentary or dramatization of fiction, a full-length play.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Advanced Scenic Design
courses.description: This course explores advanced problems in scenic design through development and critique of creative class projects and production works-in-progress.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Advanced Lighting Design
courses.description: Creative projects and topics in lighting design to develop the student’s techniques and professional practices. Work to include studies in design research, concepts, psychophysical considerations, collaboration, professional procedures and systems, paperwork, and organization. Various scales of production projects will be addressed by the student for presentation and critique and may be theoretical or productions in the departmental calendar.
courses.prerequisites_text: second- or third-year design students only; admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Advanced Costume Design
courses.description: Projects in costume design, emphasizing script analysis, research, conceptualization, and visual expression. Studio work includes costume rendering in various media for specific plays.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Special Topics in Theatre Design
courses.description: A course designed to expose the theatre design student to a variety of specialized topics, including millinery, pattern drafting and draping, scenic painting, model making, figure drawing, drafting, fitting, rendering. Topics will vary from quarter to quarter.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Design Practicum
courses.description: This course covers the artistic, aesthetic, and practical aspects of the designers’ work as they develop and execute the design toward a fully realized production.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Advanced Sound Design
courses.description: Creative projects to develop student’s techniques and professional practices. Studies include research, concepts, collaboration, professional procedures, systems and organization. Various scales of projects will be addressed for presentation and critique; may be theoretical or productions in the Department calendar.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Introduction to Doctoral Studies
courses.description: Seminar acquaints doctoral students of all levels with research methods, theoretical models, publishing protocol, professional preparation, and pedagogical approaches particular to theatre and performance studies. Course assignments are tailored to students’ scholarly interests and progress toward degree.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to PhD program in theatre or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Cultural and Critical Theory
courses.description: Selected material from following topics: Performance Theory, Dramatic Theory, Critical Theory, Cultural Studies. May be taken eight times as content varies.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to PhD program in theatre.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Acting Practicum
courses.description: This course covers the artistic, aesthetic, and practical aspects of the actors’ work as they develop and execute the character/role toward a fully realized production.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Stage Management Practicum
courses.description: Taken each term by all graduate stage management students. The class focuses on the development of knowledge and skills necessary for the contemporary stage manager. Seminar format is augmented by lab work that may include departmental productions.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: Thesis research for MFA. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Introduction to Apprentice Teaching
courses.description: This course, designed to meet the needs of the graduate students who serve as teaching assistants, includes analysis of texts and materials, discussion of teaching techniques, conducting discussion sections, formulation of topics and questions for papers, and examinations and grading. Two units = twenty-five percent TAship. Four units = fifty percent TAship.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing and consent of the instructor.

courses.subject: TDHT
courses.title: Introduction to Play Analysis
courses.description: An introduction to the fundamental techniques of analyzing dramatic texts. Focus is on the student’s ability to describe textual elements and their relationships to each other as well as on strategies for writing critically about drama.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: TDHT
courses.title: Ancient and Medieval Theatre
courses.description: Ancient and medieval theatre. Explores the roots of contemporary theatre in world performance traditions of ancient history with a focus on humans’ gravitation toward ritual and play. Examples come from Egypt, Greece, Rome, Mesoamerica, Japan, China, India, Indonesia, Persia, and England.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: TDHT
courses.title: Topics in Dramatic Literature and Theatre History
courses.description: An in-depth exposure to an important individual writer or subject in dramatic literature and/or theatre history. Topics vary from quarter to quarter. Recent courses have included Modern French Drama, and the History of Russian Theatre. No prior knowledge in theatre history is needed. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDHT
courses.title: Asian American Theatre
courses.description: This course examines pivotal dramatic works in the history of professional Asian American theatre in the United States (1960s to the present). Issues include interculturalism, the crossover between minority theatres and mainstream venues, and the performance of identity. TDHT 103 is an approved Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) course. No prior knowledge in theatre history is needed.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDHT
courses.title: History and Theory of Directing
courses.description: Evolution of directing theory from 1850 to the present with reference to the work of internationally influential directors such as Saxe-Meiningen, Antoine, Stanislavski, Meyerhold, Brecht, and Brook, among others. No prior knowledge in theatre history is needed.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDPW
courses.title: Introduction to Playwriting
courses.description: Beginning workshop in the fundamentals of playwriting. Students discuss material from a workbook that elucidates the basic principles of playwriting, do exercises designed to help them put those principles into creative practice, and are guided through the various stages of the playwriting process that culminate with in-class readings of the short plays they have completed.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: TDPW
courses.title: Screenwriting
courses.description: Basic principles of screenwriting using scenario composition, plot points, character study, story conflict, with emphasis on visual action and strong dramatic movement. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDPW 1.

courses.subject: TDPW
courses.title: Major Project in Playwriting/Screenwriting
courses.description: For the advanced student in playwriting/screenwriting. This intensive concentration in the study of playwriting and/or screenwriting will culminate in the creation of a substantial length play. A maximum of eight units of major project study, regardless of area (design, directing, stage management, playwriting) may be used to fulfill major requirements. Applicants must have completed the playwriting sequence, THPW or TDPW 1, 101, and/or consent of instructor. See department for application form.
courses.prerequisites_text: THPW or TDPW 1 and THPW or TDPW 101.

courses.subject: TDPR
courses.title: Theatre Practicum
courses.description: A production-oriented course that introduces the student to technical fundamentals of costumes, scenery, lighting, and sound for the theatre. Students will be assigned to participate on a crew for a fully mounted theatrical production supported by the department.
courses.prerequisites_text: must have department stamp.

courses.subject: TDPR
courses.title: Advanced Theatre Practicum
courses.description: A production performance-oriented course that continues the development of costume, lighting, scenery, or sound production and introduces greater responsibilities in the laboratory format. Students serve as crew heads on major departmental productions or creative projects. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDPR 6; permission of instructor; department stamp required.

courses.subject: TDPR
courses.title: Advanced Practicum in Stage Management
courses.description: A production performance-oriented course that continues the development of stage management skills and introduces greater responsibilities in the laboratory format. Students serve as either assistant stage managers on main stage productions or stage managers on studio projects. May be taken for credit up to six times for a maximum of twelve units. A maximum of eight total units may be used towards major requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDDR 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TMC
courses.title: Introduction to Public Service in America
courses.description: This course is designed to study, discuss, and analyze the history and current role of public service in the United States. Students will be introduced to the different roles held by the three sectors of the American economic structure (government, business, and nonprofit/public service) with opportunity to provide a critical analysis of those roles within American society.

courses.subject: TMC
courses.title: Partnership Schools Program Service-Learning Experience
courses.description: This service-learning experience guides undergraduates in achieving a critical and reflective understanding of the impact of historical, systemic, and institutionalized inequities on educational opportunities for underrepresented students. Undergraduates contribute to educational equity efforts by volunteering as tutors or interns at a UC San Diego Partnership School. These schools prepare first-generation youth for higher education by providing a rigorous college preparatory culture and curriculum.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: History of US Urban Communities
courses.description: This course charts the development of urban communities across the United States both temporally and geographically. It examines the patterns of cleavage, conflict, convergence of interest, and consensus that have structured urban life. Social, cultural, and economic forces will be analyzed for the roles they have played in shaping the diverse communities of America’s cities.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Urban World System
courses.description: Examines cities and the environment in a global context. Emphasizes how the world’s economy and the earth’s ecology are increasingly interdependent. Focuses on biophysical and ethicosocial concerns rooted in the contemporary division of labor among cities, Third World industrialization, and the post-industrial transformation of US cities.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
courses.description: This course provides an entry-level introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and using GIS to make decisions: acquiring data and organizing data in useful formats, demographic mapping, and geocoding.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Introduction to the Real Estate and Development Process
courses.description: This course introduces students to the terminology, concepts, and basic practices of real estate finance and development. It surveys real estate law, appraisal, marketing, brokerage, management, finance, investment analysis, and taxation.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Applied Urban Economics for Planning and Development
courses.description: This course explores how economics contributes to understanding and solving urban problems using a “learn by doing” approach. Economic analysis will be applied to important issues that planners and developers must deal with, such as land markets, housing, and zoning.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Real Estate and Development Principles and Analysis
courses.description: This course will analyze the concepts related to the planning, development, leasing, valuation, and financing of real estate. There will be special emphasis on critical thinking and analytical decision-making by solving real estate problems primarily using Excel and Argus.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Real Estate and Development Colloquium
courses.description: In this course, students will attend weekly seminars presented by leading researchers and practitioners in the field of real estate and development. Students will learn about best practices and innovative case studies from the field. Recommended for students interested in the real estate and development minor or major. Enrollment restricted to RED (US27) and USP (US26) majors and minors only.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: The Practice of Planning Research
courses.description: A hands-on introduction to observational research and data analysis in urban studies and planning, emphasizing tools and techniques used to solve real-world planning problems. Special emphasis on statistics and quantitative reasoning, including discussion of their limits.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Urban Sociology
courses.description: (Same as SOCI 153.) Introduces students to the major approaches in the sociological study of cities and to what a sociological analysis can add to our understanding of urban processes.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Planning Theories
courses.description: This course is designed to explore major theories of urban and spatial planning. Topics include the role of the planner in a diverse society, the relationship between knowledge and action, and the implications of planning practices for social and spatial justice.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Land Use Planning
courses.description: Introduction to land use planning in the United States: zoning and subdivision, regulation, growth management, farmland preservation, environmental protection, and comprehensive planning. May be coscheduled with USP 224.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: The Design of Social Research
courses.description: Research methods are tools for improving knowledge. Beginning with a research question, students will learn to select appropriate methods for sampling, collecting, and analyzing data to improve their research activities and research results.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor. Enrollment restricted to USP (US26) majors and minors only.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Community Organizing
courses.description: Provides an overview of community organizing and considers organizing as both a tactical and strategic approach to effective community building and leadership development. Examines how various communities have approached collaborative leadership, organizing, and community building.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Life Course Scholars Research and Core Fundamentals
courses.description: This course introduces students to major concepts, demographic trends, and the diversity of the aging experience. Through site visits, community-based research, and interactions with elders, students will understand the social and structural determinants of health and well-being across the life course.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor and department approval. This is an application-based course.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: The US Health-Care System
courses.description: This course will provide an overview of the organization of health care within the context of the community with emphasis on the political, social, and cultural influences. It is concerned with the structure, objectives, and trends of major health and health-related programs in the United States to include sponsorship, financing, training and utilization of health personnel.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Environmental and Preventive Health Issues
courses.description: This course will analyze needs of populations, highlighting current major public health problems such as chronic and communicable diseases, environmental hazards of diseases, psychiatric problems and additional diseases, new social mores affecting health maintenance, consumer health awareness and health practices, special needs of economically and socially disadvantaged populations. The focus is on selected areas of public and environmental health, namely: epidemiology, preventive services in family health, communicable and chronic disease control, and occupational health.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Real Estate and Development Law and Regulation
courses.description: This course reviews the legal issues, processes, and institutions involved in real estate. Topics include principles of real property law, legislative and judicial institutions, land use and environmental regulation, financial instruments, property transactions, and forms of investment and development entities. Prerequisites : upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Real Estate Planning and Development
courses.description: This course covers the methods and procedures utilized in development from inception to completion. Topics include initial planning, project feasibility and decision-making, partnerships, financing, design, entitlement and approvals, site acquisition, construction management, project completion, leasing, and asset management. Prerequisites : USP 5 and upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Advanced Real Estate Development Finance and Investment
courses.description: The course will examine various case studies of real-life development and investment projects, including apartments, acquisition of a distressed project, office development, land development, and student housing. The students will also incorporate zoning analysis and joint venture structures into the case studies where appropriate. Prerequisites : USP 152 or USP 152A.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Real Estate and Development Market Analysis
courses.description: This course examines the analysis of demand for real estate products and site-specific real estate development projects. Consideration is given to relevant factors such as economic change, social attitudes, and changing laws. Prerequisites : upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Environmental Design and Crime Prevention
courses.description: This course is an introduction to theories and concepts relating to the built and natural environment and crime prevention. Perspectives from planners and criminologists will be discussed, and a real-world project will be used to integrate theory into practice.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Advanced Special Topics in Transportation
courses.description: Transportation topics may include policies such as congestion pricing, transit districts, street parking, or road safety regulation; social and legal implications of new transportation technologies; or methods for analyzing transit behavior. Topics may vary. May be taken for credit up to three times. May be coscheduled with USP 265C.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Planning for Sustainable Communities
courses.description: This course will explore the different factors and processes that shape a sustainable city. Contemporary green planning techniques and values will be evaluated. The course will also discuss planning, designing, and implementation of sustainable facilities that will reduce sprawl.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Sustainable Development
courses.description: Sustainable development is invoked by a wide range of actors and sectors that seek to promote environmentally sound and socially just approaches to economic development. This course critically examines the diverse, and often contradictory, definitions and applications of sustainability throughout the world. May be coscheduled with USP 271.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Site Analysis
courses.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of context-sensitive site analysis, including regulatory framework, site inventory, site selection and programming, and conceptual design. Demonstrates use of planning and development tools to conduct suitability analysis and project visualization in real world settings. Enrollment restricted to USP (US26) and RED (US27) majors and minors only.
courses.prerequisites_text: USP 124, upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Urban Design Practicum
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce the student to the theory and practice of urban design, the form of the built environment, and how it is created. There is an emphasis on the development within a larger urban context. Renumbered from USP 177. Students may not receive credit for USP 177A and USP 177.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Public Transportation
courses.description: Livable cities rely on balanced transportation systems that can mitigate the negative impacts of car-oriented environment and society. This course will explore the role of public transit in creating a balanced transportation system. A variety of public transportation systems will be analyzed.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Real Estate Finance and Development Studio I
courses.description: This course introduces students to the challenges of developing and financing real property. Students work in teams to prepare a proposal for a complete site-specific project that incorporates real estate finance, development, and design.
courses.prerequisites_text: USP 5, USP 15, USP 25, USP 50, USP 124, USP 151, USP 152A, and USP 153. Restricted to seniors within the Real Estate and Development major. (Only offered fall quarter.)

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Senior Sequence Research Proposal
courses.description: Introduces students to the theory and practice of social research including the challenges of writing a scholarly proposal. Students are required to complete one hundred hours of an internship experience while critically examining the relations between social science and society.
courses.prerequisites_text: USP 30, USP 60, USP 124, one USP technical elective, and one USP Research Methods course. Restricted to seniors within the Urban Studies and Planning major. (Only offered fall quarter.)

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Special Topics in Urban Planning
courses.description: An undergraduate course designed to cover various aspects of Urban Planning. May be taken for credit up to two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Intermediate GIS for Urban and Community Planning
courses.description: Intermediate geographic information systems (GIS) as applied to urban studies builds upon the introductory course and teaches students how to use the GIS software, collect and analyze data, and produce maps and products relating to demographics, transportation, health, public safety, and other current issues.
courses.prerequisites_text: USP 4 and upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: San Diego Community Research
courses.description: Using the San Diego region as a case study, students will be introduced to the process of collecting, evaluating, and presenting urban and regional data using a variety of methods, including aggregate data analysis, historical research, and ethnography.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Research Seminar in Washington, DC
courses.description: (Same as COGS 194, COMM 194, HITO 193, POLI 194, SOCI 194, SIO 194.) Course attached to six-unit internship taken by students participating in the UCDC Program. Involves weekly seminar meetings with faculty and teaching assistant and a substantial research paper.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval and participating in UCDC Program.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Pedagogy and Learning Apprenticeship
courses.description: Under the supervision of an instructor, undergraduate students gain teaching experience through practical experiences in course management and effective teaching methods. May be taken for credit up to three times for a maximum of eight units.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study on a topic or in a field not included in the regular departmental curriculum by special arrangement with a faculty member.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Advanced Special Topics in Transportation
courses.description: Transportation topics may include policies such as congestion pricing, transit districts, street parking, or road safety regulation; social and legal implications of new transportation technologies; or methods for analyzing transit behavior. Topics may vary. May be taken for credit up to three times. May be coscheduled with USP 165C.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: USP
courses.title: Sustainable Development
courses.description: Sustainable development is invoked by a wide range of actors and sectors that seek to promote environmentally sound and socially just approaches to economic development. This course critically examines the diverse, and often contradictory, definitions and applications of sustainability throughout the world. May be coscheduled with USP 171.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Introduction to Art Making: Two-Dimensional Practices
courses.description: An introduction to the concepts and techniques of two-dimensional art making with an emphasis on drawing. Lectures will introduce skills and concepts of contemporary drawing practice in relation to a variety of genres such as illustration, comics, advertising, animation, and other forms of visualization. This course is offered only one time each year.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Introduction to Art in Europe and America
courses.description: This course examines the history of Western art and architecture through such defining issues as the respective roles of tradition and innovation in the production and appreciation of art; the relation of art to its broader intellectual and historical contexts; and the changing concepts of the monument, the artist, meaning, style, and “art” itself. Representative examples will be selected from different periods, ranging from antiquity to modern. Content will vary with the instructor.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Seminar in Art History Methods
courses.description: This course, a lower-division seminar for art history majors, covers the research tools and fundamental skills needed for advanced work in the field. Topics include descriptive and analytical writing; revision and peer review; compiling annotated bibliographies with traditional and online resources, indexes, and databases; evaluating source materials (including those found online); defining research programs; and preparing and delivering art history presentations.
courses.prerequisites_text: none. Art history majors only.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Introduction to Speculative Design
courses.description: Speculative design uses design methods to question and investigate material culture with critical creative purpose. This course provides a historical, theoretical, and methodological introduction to speculative design as a distinct program. Emphasis is tracing the integration of interdisciplinary intellectual and technical problems toward creative, unexpected propositions and prototypes.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Design Communication
courses.description: This course provides a strong foundation in contemporary techniques of design communication, introduced in light of their significance to visual culture and the speculative design field. We cover digital image editing, typography, vector-based illustration and diagramming, and document layout. Also introduced are basic digital video editing tools and web production formats. Emphasis is on mastery of craft through iteration and presentation of multiple projects.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Introduction to Creative Coding
courses.description: This course provides students with a foundation in programming and computational thinking, and their application in creative projects. Topics covered may include generative graphics and sound, interactive media, and others. Students will gain practical skills through hands-on experience and experimentation, learning to integrate computing into artistic practices.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Introduction to Digital Photography
courses.description: An in-depth exploration of the camera and image utilizing photographic digital technology. Emphasis is placed on developing fundamental control of the processes and materials through lectures, field, and lab experience. Basic discussion of image making included. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: none. Open to visual arts majors and minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Introduction to Media
courses.description: Operating as both a lecture and production course, this introductory class provides a technical foundation and theoretical context for all subsequent production-oriented film and video studies. In the laboratory, the student will learn the basic skills necessary to initiate video production. Completion of Visual Arts 70N is necessary to obtain a media card. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: none. Open to visual arts and cinematic arts majors and minors.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Introduction to the Studio Major
courses.description: A practical introduction to the studio art major and a conceptual introduction to how diverse strategies of art making are produced, analyzed, and critiqued. Introduces historical and contemporary topics in painting, drawing, sculpture, installation, and performance art and field-based practices. Required for all studio majors and minors including transfer students. Must be taken in residence at UC San Diego.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Media History
courses.description: A survey of media history and theory across a range of national and international contexts. Offers historically situated analysis of print, audio, text-based, image-based, and time-based media art and design in narrative, avant-garde, and documentary forms across different movements, genres, and styles with attention to associated theories and conventions (such as mechanical, electronic, graphical, lens-based, video, digital, and mixed media). Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Introduction to Public Culture
courses.description: This course examines contemporary theories and concepts of public culture and social practice, including new spheres of public culture design research and practice that intervene across urban socioeconomic and political domains, environmental, spatial and community-based dynamics, architecture, information design, and visualization.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Design of Public Culture
courses.description: This course will explore and develop designs and strategies that engage today’s shifting public domain structures and their various spatial and systematic manifestations. The problematic of “the public” and the politics of public sphere are situated as sites of investigation through which we imagine new interfaces between individuals, collectives, and institutions with the aim of coproducing more critical and inclusive forms of public space and culture.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 100.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: History of Speculative Design: Projects, Programs, and Practices
courses.description: This course surveys the history of speculative design in a planetary context, introducing students to important and diverse projects and design practices. These may include experimental architecture, science fiction literature, speculative software design, critical object and installation, philosophy of technology, alternative futures, graphical and interaction design, and more. Emphasis will be on understanding projects and practices in historical, cultural, and political context. Prerequisites : upper-division standing.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Drawing: Representing the Subject
courses.description: A studio course in beginning drawing covering basic drawing and composition. These concepts will be introduced by the use of models, still life, landscapes, and conceptual projects.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 80.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Drawing: Practices and Genre
courses.description: A continuation of VIS 105A. A studio course in which the student will investigate a wider variety of technical and conceptual issues involved in contemporary art practice related to drawing.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 105A.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Drawing: Portfolio Projects
courses.description: A studio course in drawing, emphasizing individual creative problems. Class projects, discussions, and critiques will focus on issues related to intention, subject matter, and context.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 105B.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Painting: Image Making
courses.description: A studio course focusing on problems inherent in painting—transferring information and ideas onto a two-dimensional surface, color, composition, as well as manual and technical procedures. These concepts will be explored through the use of models, still life, and landscapes.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 80.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Painting: Practices and Genre
courses.description: A continuation of VIS 106A. A studio course in which the student will investigate a wider variety of technical and conceptual issues involved in contemporary art practice related to painting.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 106A.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Sculpture: Making the Object
courses.description: A studio course focusing on the problems involved in transferring ideas and information into three-dimensions. Course will explore materials and construction as dictated by the intended object. Specific problems to be investigated will be determined by the individual professor.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 80.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Sculpture: Portfolio Projects
courses.description: A studio course in sculpture emphasizing individual creative problems. Class projects, discussions, and critiques will focus on issues related to intention, subject matter, and context. Students may not receive credit for both VIS 107C and VIS 107CN.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 107B.

courses.subject: VIS
courses.title: Advanced Projects in Art
